profile: Stock PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2 under the native UTF-8 profile. Explicitly named plain partitioned indexes and explicitly named physical indexes on attached leaves are declared in the same local catalog.
scope: Resolve one named btree index on a partitioned branch or attached leaf. A nonphysical branch selects only the attached physical index lineage. An attached heap's named physical index is rebuilt as a single index.

Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.role: Absolute resolved named index reference and its physical partition role.
Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.structure: Immutable schema, index and owning table identifiers, and PartitionRebuildKind.
Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.conditions: The owner and index share a persistent local application namespace and different relation names. The analyzer must identify the exact declared branch or leaf index. Ordinary removal must refuse this restricted role.
Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.meaning: Rebuild the exact named physical index or physical descendants of this index's attachment lineage. The referenced heap's other indexes and its TOAST indexes remain unchanged.
Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.sql: Independently quote the schema and index positions. The same external declared identity retains its branch or leaf semantics.
Schema/Index/Partition/PartitionIndexRef.externalInterpretation: Use the same local named index, owner, native attached index lineage and language profile.

amendedConstructors.Schema/Index/ReindexIndex: Admit the separately typed partition index reference as a third closed target role. Keep the same mode and grammar anchor.

rules: Native standard and concurrent branch rebuilds require a top-level command. A standard physical leaf rebuild can be rolled back.
Rebuild only the selected physical index lineage across schemas. Preserve all other index storage, TOAST relations, heap rows, ownership and attachment edges.
A standard physical rebuild retains the index OID. A concurrent physical rebuild can replace it and relink the resulting index to the same owner and parent coordinates.
An empty partitioned index lineage can be a valid rebuild with no physical effects.
observations: Exact named index, owning table and branch or leaf tag in both construction routes.
Native result, transaction state, indexed positions, physical OID and storage change relations and complete declared parent links.
Cross-schema attached leaves, untouched other named indexes and auxiliary TOAST storage, rows and rollback.

finite.identity: Consume all 40 coordinates in both direct and analyzed construction on each pinned native release.

exploration.domain: Vary empty and populated partitions, branch scope and attached physical selection, quoted names, ordered native concurrency options, distinct unaffected indexes and transaction state.

negative: Ordinary DROP INDEX given a branch
Ordinary DROP INDEX given a physical leaf target
Direct identical index and owner names
faults: Publish the branch through the leaf role
Rebuild only one attached physical child
Change the selector to a table and rebuild unrelated and auxiliary indexes
trust: Named declarations and index kind, closed resolved target types, exact PHP route audit, stock index and heap catalog observations and independent replay.
open: Implicitly named indexes, partitioned constraint-owned indexes and incomplete hierarchy declarations require additional rules and evidence.
